01. 1.

Learned counsel Mr. S. Sarangi submits that he has entered appearance by filing Vakalatanama on behalf of the Informant.
2.
Registry is requested to verify the same and reflect the name of learned counsel appearing for the Informant, Mr. Sarangi in the file, cause list as well as web portal of this Court.

3. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.
4.

The Petitioners are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with C.T. No.1494 of 2025 pending on the file of learned J.M.F.C.-II, Bhubaneswar arising out of Infocity P.S. Case No.431 of 2025 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 126(2)/ 351(2)/ 115(2)/ 117(2)/ 296/ 304(2)/
3(5) of BNS.
5.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the Petitioners that omnibus allegations have been made and the occurrence has taken place during immersion function without any premeditation.

Hence,
the Petitioners may be protected by pre-arrest bail.

1 6.
Learned counsel for the Informant opposes the pre-arrest bail and submits that he has suffered injury for which he had undergo treatment in KIMS Hospital.
7. On perusal of the Case Diary which refers to the injury report, it is seen that the injury of the informant is simple in nature.
8. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for pre-arrest bail during the currency of investigation.

9. It is brought to the notice of this Court that Petitioner No.1 has following criminal antecedents;
"i. Infocity P.S. Case No.420 dt.04.09.2025, U/s.126(2)/ 296/ 115(2)/ 117(2)/ 109/ 303(2)/ 351(2)/
3(5) of BNS ii. Infocity P.S. Case No.422 dt.04.09.2025, U/s.126(2)/ 296/ 115(2)/ 117(2)/ 109/
303(2)/ 351(2)/ 3(5) of BNS iii. Infocity P.S. Case No.428 dt.05.09.2025, U/s.126(2)/ 296/ 115(2)/
304(2)/ 351(2)/ 3(5) of BNS iv. Chandaka P.S. Case No.139 dt.30.09.2018, U/s.341/ 294/ 323/ 324/
325/ 307/ 354/ 506/ 34 of IPC"
10.

So far as the criminal antecedents of the Petitioner No.1 is concerned, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that from the date of registration of the cases it can be seen that the same relates to the self-same incident.
Hence, the criminal antecedents ought not to deter this Court from considering the prayer of Petitioner No.1 for pre-arrest bail.
11. Considering the rival submission, this Court is not inclined to entertain the application for pre-arrest bail in respect of Petitioner No.1.

However, in the event the Petitioner No.1 surrenders before the learned Court in seisin in the aforesaid case and moves an application for his release on bail, the same shall be considered on its own merit.

12. So far as ABLAPL in respect of Petitioner No.2 is concerned, this Court directs that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner No.2 shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper subject to verification of criminal antecedent of similar nature.
13. If it comes to the fore that the Petitioner No.2 has any such criminal antecedent, this order shall not be given effect to.
14. It is needless to state that the Petitioner No.2 shall cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
15. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.
16. U.C.C. as per rules.
(V. NARASINGH)
